identity.issuer: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC (self-generated internal log)

scan.summary: This is a daily pre-shift inspection log for a single propane-powered forklift (unit FL-2, Toyota 8FGU25) at the Portland warehouse, recording tick-mark checks against a fixed safety checklist for each shift in September 2026. It is evidence, not a rulebook: it shows whether the required daily examination under OSHA's powered industrial truck standard is actually being done and whether defects are being caught and handled.
scan.freshness_note: The log's entries run from September 1 through September 17, 2026, with no entries for the ten days since (today is September 27, 2026). For a daily-use requirement, a gap of this length means the company cannot currently show inspection evidence for the most recent workdays; ask for the continuation pages or confirm whether the truck was taken out of service.

gaps.title: No entries after September 17
gaps.description: The table stops at Sep 17 (hours 4,886); there are no logged inspections for the remaining workdays of September, up to today's date.
gaps.fix: Obtain and file the continuation of this log through the end of September, or confirm and document that unit FL-2 was out of service/not used during that period.

gaps.title: No documented follow-up on Sep 9 horn defect
gaps.description: The Sep 9 row shows an X (defect) for the horn with the note 'Horn not working,' yet the truck was still logged with hours that day, and the Sep 10 entry simply shows the horn as OK again with no repair record, work order, or out-of-service notation in between.
gaps.fix: Keep a corrective-action or maintenance record (repair ticket, out-of-service tag, or note in this log) showing the truck was pulled from service and the horn repaired before Sep 10 use, so the file demonstrates defects are 'immediately reported and corrected' rather than just re-passing the next day.

deadlines.title: Daily pre-shift examination of unit FL-2 before use
deadlines.source_line: Inspection per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.

facts.affects: Confirms the identity of the specific truck this daily-examination requirement applies to at the Portland site.

version_of.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log — Unit FL-2 (Toyota 8FGU25), Portland Warehouse, September 2026

expected_missing.title: Formal operator training/evaluation records for M.C. and J.R.
expected_missing.why: The log names two operators by initials, but a company running a forklift program would normally also hold documented initial and (every three years) refresher evaluations for each named operator under 29 CFR 1910.178(l); this log alone doesn't show that.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Maintenance/repair work order tied to the Sep 9 horn defect
expected_missing.why: Companies that run daily inspection logs like this one typically also keep a maintenance ticket or vendor repair record whenever the log flags a defect, to show the truck was actually fixed and not just re-checked the next day.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Periodic (e.g., annual or manufacturer-interval) mechanical inspection records
expected_missing.why: Daily pre-shift logs are usually paired with less-frequent, more thorough maintenance inspections performed by a mechanic or dealer, which this document does not include.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

scan.confidence_notes: The single page is clear and fully legible, and the cited standard (29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7)) matches OSHA's actual daily-examination and 'remove from service if unsafe' requirement, confirmed against current OSHA/eCFR text. My uncertainty is entirely about what happened outside the page: whether the horn was actually repaired before Sep 10, and whether inspections continued after Sep 17 on pages not provided.
